set.body:
Outcome:
Add an additive, requirement-driven first-level summary interface so upstream second-level consumers request exactly the linear estimates and uncertainty they need. Preserve existing LinearModel/GlsModel/Fit/FitView behavior. Planning complete; implementation has not started.

Scope / non-goals:
fmrireg owns numerical summary preparation/execution; fmrimod resolves scientific subject/run/contrast specifications, schedules cohorts and chooses retention; fmridataset owns disk access and spatial identity. Do not introduce a parallel fast solver or silently change model/AR/censor/rank policy. NIfTI implementation, group estimators, projection caches and persistent sessions are staged follow-ons, not prerequisites for the first useful output path. No publication is authorized.

Chosen public contract (proposed names):
OutputSpec { estimands: EstimandSet, uncertainty: Uncertainty::{None, Marginal, Joint} }. Named contrast matrices and selected coefficients are convenience constructors for linear functionals L. fmrimod binds stable scientific IDs to subject-specific design columns; units, coding, normalization and run aggregation are part of that binding. Labels alone never establish cross-subject equivalence. fmrireg accepts the resolved matrix and binding, avoiding any dependency on the formula/design crate.
LinearModel and GlsModel gain prepare_outputs(spec) -> PreparedOutputs, with workspace(max_features), run_into(data, workspace), and checked workspace-byte reporting. Runtime requests have a closed SummaryView::{Estimates, Marginal, Joint} result plus an owned counterpart preserving immutable schema and numerical context. All variants expose estimates; uncertainty capabilities require the appropriate variant. Existing fit APIs keep their full-fit semantics and compatibility.
No t/F/p calculation is implied by requesting uncertainty. Statistics remain explicit consumers. A later compiled contrast kernel may replace coefficient-then-contrast execution only after numerical qualification.

Uncertainty representation:
e_v = L beta_v; Cov(e_v | fixed W) = sigma2_v G; G = L V0 L^T. Marginal stores diag(G) and one residual-scale value per feature; Joint stores the shared q-by-q G and feature scales. Accessors return actual variance/SE or explicitly materialize covariance, avoiding confusion with unit covariance. Include residual df, scale definition and conditional estimated-noise provenance. Joint means covariance between requested estimates at the same feature, not spatial covariance or across-subject covariance. The shared-G encoding applies only when design/whitening/selected rows are common across that feature block; per-voxel differing geometry must use another representation or be rejected explicitly.
Finite zero residual variance and zero linear functionals are valid new summaries with zero variance/SE. Legacy t/F degeneracy rules remain unchanged. Dependent estimand rows yield valid positive-semidefinite, possibly singular joint covariance; do not reuse F-test independence checks for summary preparation. Selected coefficient summaries must be estimable; legacy raw minimum-norm coefficients remain available through Fit. No hidden variance flooring, dropping, regularization, or IID substitution.

Compute versus retention:
OutputSpec states required results. Session retention policy separately states whether to retain only those outputs, coefficients, coefficient-plus-scale summaries or future projections. Private kernel selection chooses how to produce their union. A contrast-plus-SE request requires full-model residual scale but not retained/exported all-beta maps. The first safe implementation may compute p-by-block coefficient scratch and explicit residual RSS, then discard those betas. This is a memory/output reduction, not a claim that all full-model arithmetic disappears. Estimates-only omits RSS and prediction entirely; any necessary initial residual work for feasible-GLS noise estimation remains. Plan inspection should report requested outputs, residual-scale dependency, scratch/retained byte counts and selected kernel, without promising unmeasured timings.
Multiple consumer requests share model work and RSS without changing any request's definition. Stronger cached summaries may satisfy weaker requests. Marginal summaries do not generally provide uncertainty for a new combination; Joint supports combinations within the retained estimand span. No cache promotion invents discarded information.

Relevant paths:
crates/fmrireg/src/lib.rs: LinearModel::new, fit_buffers_validated, check_contrast, FitView::{t_contrast,f_contrast}, GlsModel.
crates/fmrireg/src/workspace.rs: current fixed full-fit buffers and byte accounting.
crates/fmrireg/src/dataset.rs: public sealed BlockModel, BoundModel observation IDs, ordered reusable worker executor.
crates/fmrireg/src/selection.rs and selected_estimation.rs: selected-row and feasible-GLS contracts.
crates/fmri-noise/src/lib.rs: custom WhiteningPlan compatibility.
crates/fmrimod/src/lib.rs: composition boundary; group audit tracked separately in bd-01M5YK74R39H0EF9BMFSX58GND.

Implementation stages / acceptance gates:
1. Output contract and reference adapter. Add src/output.rs with validated estimands, uncertainty levels, immutable schema/context, borrowed/owned summaries, and model.prepare_outputs. Initially execute via the existing fit path. Share pure estimability/covariance logic independently of t/F validation. Prove estimates, variances, SEs and cross-covariances against analytic/current R fixtures; dependent and zero estimands; zero variance; nonestimable coefficient selectors; consistent subject/run bindings. The public contract is useful even before new speed kernels.
2. Minimal work per request. Add estimates-only execution using existing pseudoinverse and explicit whitening, omit prediction/RSS buffers, keep uncertainty paths on explicit residuals. Introduce private workspace/kernel abstraction providing checked bytes, allocation, execution and view reconstruction. Preserve public BlockModel through adapters; hidden methods remain public API. Workers return owned workspaces and the sink reconstructs borrowed outputs. Test exact budget boundaries, full/tail blocks, strides, invalid input/error recovery, custom whitening, no unrequested retained all-beta outputs, and allocation differences. Verify output validity on its own required graph rather than demanding errors from computations not requested.
3. Upstream requirements and reuse. Add fmrimod integration that compiles consumer needs to OutputSpec, validates all scientific IDs/units/run aggregation before data reads, and stores immutable owned summaries. Independent univariate variance-aware reducers request Marginal; coupled outcomes request Joint according to their actual consumer contract. Implement request unions, cache capability checks and invalidation keys for data/preprocessing, selected rows/order, feature geometry, design, noise, rank/numerical policy and output schema. Backend enters reproducibility receipts. Custom whitening has no durable identity by default; explicit deterministic/version contract is required. Coordinate with existing group audit; do not implement group estimators here.
4. Qualify direct contrast projection. Candidate K=L(WX)+ applied to explicitly whitened data, estimates-only first. Compare full entrywise results, strong cancellation/near-collinearity/large-offset tests and portable/Accelerate paths; never compose W into K or use unsafe RSS norm subtraction/in-place GEMM by default. Retain only workloads/guards supported by evidence; existing correct path is fallback. q=1/4/16 across n=300/1200 and p=8/32 (larger designs only when justified), record warm compute, cold/read cost separately, memory and threads.
5. Later projection/session pipeline. Extract shared private factorization/inference metadata only when temporal projection requires it. Keep original selected n distinct from projection r; df=n-rank(requested model). Preserve dictionary span and rank policy, original coefficient coordinates, stable complement energy and immutable basis/noise/data bindings. Then persistent cohort scheduler, additive fallible fmridataset file opening, and NIfTI/cache integration. These extend PreparedOutputs rather than add new scientific output modes. Incremental basis and variable-AR projections remain research candidates.

Verification commands (run when implementing, not run for this plan):
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/fmrimod-output-target cargo test -p fmrireg -p fmri-noise --all-features
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/fmrimod-output-target cargo test -p fmrireg --no-default-features
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/fmrimod-output-target cargo clippy -p fmrireg -p fmri-noise --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p fmrireg -p fmri-noise --check
Add fmrimod integration tests when stage3 changes it. Snapshot source/input/reference hashes, record numerical tolerances and independent build/check exit statuses. Benchmark equivalent requested outputs and distinguish computation, retained results and backend scratch. Regression expectations include unchanged rank/df/estimability and borrowed lifetime protection.

Risks / escalation:
Uncertainty summaries must not silently represent unconditional AR-estimation uncertainty. Contrast-dependent rows are allowed, but tests or mixed-effects consumers can have stricter invertibility/positive-variance requirements. General persistent cache support for custom mutable whitening is unsafe without a contract. Any arithmetic reassociation needs adverse-case qualification against the established numerical path. No speedup claims until measured.

Next action:
Implement stage1 only as the first reviewable slice, then stage2. Inspect current Git/Mote claims before implementation; unrelated active work must be preserved. User requested a plan in this turn, not production changes.
set.title: Implement requirement-driven first-level estimates and uncertainty summaries
